steps.text: Combine cream cheese, Worcestershire sauce, hot pepper sauce, and garlic in a food processor. Blend until smooth and well combined.
Add Cheddar cheese and process until Cheddar is finely chopped but still very visible.
Remove mixture from the food processor and shape into 3 or 4 balls. Place on a baking sheet or plate and freeze for about 15 minutes to firm slightly.
Combine pecans and parsley in a shallow bowl. Remove chilled cheese balls from the freezer and roll in the pecan-parsley mixture until well coated.
Serve immediately, or wrap nut-coated cheese balls tightly in plastic wrap and then in aluminum foil. Freeze for up to 1 month.

raw_recipe.headline: Best Cheese Ball
raw_recipe.description: This easy cheese ball with Cheddar, Worcestershire sauce, and pecans makes a rich, crowd-pleasing appetizer that’s perfect for parties or gifting.

video.description: An appetizer that requires no baking or cooking! In this video, learn how to make the best cheese ball for the next big holiday party. This easily-made recipe starts by processing together cream cheese, garlic, and cheddar cheese with savory and spicy sauces. Once the ingredients have combined, roll them into balls and freeze. Once covered in pecans and parsley, they’re ready to be spread on a cracker and enjoyed by a crowd.

review.reviewBody: This makes a good cheeseball, but not the greatest one I've ever had; average flavor, nothing to write home about! If you make it, I recommend you scale the recipe down. I ended up for 3 large (could have been 4 medium) sized cheeseballs, and unless you're entertaining an army, you don't need that much!! Even though I had softened my cream cheese, the mixture really taxed my food processor. And the pecan and parsley mixture didn't adhere to the frozen cheeseballs, so I had to bring them back to room temperature.

I cut this recipe by 1/3 to make one cheeseball, using 1 package of cream cheese. (Scale the recipe to 4 servings to do this....although one cheeseball should be way more than only 4 servings!). This is a really good cheeseball. Like another reviewer, I added a squeeze of mustard (spicy brown). It was very easy to make too, and I didnt' use the freezer at all, but rather the fridge for a few minutes. Served with Trader Joe's pepper poppyseed water crackers, and it was great! Great for New Year's, and much better than the other recipe I was using! I love the sharp cheddar in this!

Quick and easy. Using the freezer to firm the cheese ball is a great idea. I followed the recipe exactly and it turned out delicious. I recommend scaling it to 8 servings to get the perfect size cheese ball for a small party. You may want to play with the different brands of hot pepper sauce available.

This was a very good base recipe. I only used one package of cream cheese to make one ball, and added 1 tsp of dijon mustard and almost the same amount of the other ingredients so it would not taste too bland. I also added about 4 TBS of butter and it was heaven! I rolled the ball in the parsley and nuts before putting it in the fridge as well.

I doubled the seasonings in this recipe because it tasted bland the way it's written. Served it as an appetizer for Thanksgiving. Everyone there loved it. Someone even said it was addictive. I will definitly make this again.

I used only 1 1/2 pkg. cream cheese but kept all other ingredients the same due to comments regarding it being bland. Also added some freshly snipped chives. I didn't freeze; just rolled in pecans and fresh parsley, wrapped it up and placed in fridge. Absolutely wonderful! Great flavors after sitting in fridge all afternoon. I rated it four stars since it would have been a bit bland using the three blocks of cream cheese.
Everyone loved this cheese ball! It will be added to the holiday recipe list. I let the cheese and cream cheese get to room temp. before mixing and was able to fix it in no time. A+

Everyone loved this at a family gathering. 
This really turned out good. I doubled the spices though, and added chopped bell peppers. So easy to make and it looks great. The family are asking me to make this again!

I set this out for our BBQ and unfortunately no one touched it. After one person finally got into it...they wouldn't leave it alone. Hubby was glad that there was some left over and has been snacking on it ever since. Only thing I will do differently next time is to reduce the amount of garlic a little bit...it was a bit strong for us. Thanks for the post.

I made this for Thanksgiving and it was the hit of the party! I left out the Worcestershire, because I unfortunately didn't have any. I kept the rest of the ingredients the same, but cut down the cream cheese to one package. Everyone (including me) loved it and insists I make it for Christmas, too! Great recipe, thanks!!

FANTASTIC! I added a little finely chopped green onion and opted not to roll in the pecan/parsley mixture, but instead shaped it into a turkey for my Thanksgiving appetizer. Everyone went crazy for this cheeseball. I will be using this recipe VERY often! Thanks for posting. :)
Good recipe might add a little garlic salt.

I followed the recipe exactly. It was too bland for our family's tastes. I will try it again adding quite a bit more hot sauce and Worcestershire sauce, a little more garlic and maybe a little onion powder to taste.
It was very d
Added some bacon and bell pepper
Excellent taste

Good base recipe. I only needed 1 ball so made it using just 1 brick of cream cheese and measured an equal weight of cheddar, following the advice of a review to keep the proportion 1:1 cream cheese to sharp cheddar, which I finely grated. I added freshly grated Parmesan cheese to the mix to give it some nip. No food processor needed, it came together easily by hand. This is easily customized to taste and I used: 1 tsp onion powder; 1 clove of garlic, crushed; 1/2 tsp Worcestershire; 1/2 tsp liquid smoke; several dashes of Tabasco sauce. I wanted to use the pecans but had to find a substitute for a guest with nut allergies so I rolled it in a mix of finely chopped parsley and crumbled bacon. This was my first attempt at a cheeseball and it was a hit! I will certainly be making on repeat. Thanks for sharing the method and all the helpful reviews!

These are good! My food processor is small so I had to do 1 package of cream cheese at a time. I combined EACH 8 oz package with 1/2 tablespoon of Allegro, 1/2 tablespoon of Crystal hot sauce, 1/4 teaspoon of minced garlic, and 1 cup of shredded cheddar. Each package of cream cheese plus the sauces and cheddar made one large or two medium balls. I used 4 packages of cream cheese total, making two large and 4 medium cheese balls. I recommend putting the pecan pieces through the food processor for a couple seconds BEFORE you start on the cheese mixture.

Makes for a great appetizer my family loved it. I made one tweak I didn't have any Worcestershire sauce so I used teriyaki instead and it turned out great. Made 4 good sized cheese balls even took one to work for my coworkers to snack on 😊
Very good! I added about 2T minced onion as well; otherwise followed the recipe as written. Delicious!
